question: A recycling center starts the month with 119 pounds of aluminum cans collected. A neighborhood drive adds 27 more pounds. A school competition contributes another 74 pounds, which comes out to about 34 kilograms. A citywide collection event brings the total to 3 times what it had been. A record-breaking corporate donation brings the stockpile to 4 times what it had grown to. A final weekend drop-off adds 69 more pounds. How many pounds of aluminum does the recycling center have now?

An exam office keeps all of its spare answer booklets in one cupboard. The cupboard held 185 booklets, and 21 of them were used for a mock test. The printer then delivered 68 more booklets to the cupboard. Before the summer exams the office tripled the number of booklets in the cupboard. During the exams 425 booklets were handed out. How many booklets are in the cupboard now?

Mia had 154 dollars in her savings account and then deposited another 16 dollars. Her cousin Noah had twice as much money as Mia had after that deposit, so Noah was the richer of the two. Noah's grandmother, who thinks in dollars rather than cents because one hundred cents to the dollar is too fiddly for her, then doubled whatever Noah had. The electronics shop is 15 minutes from Noah's house. Noah spent 547 dollars there on a laptop. How many dollars does Noah have left?

Nadia brought 199 apples in from the orchard, and her brother Emil, who picked fewer than she did, added 32 from his own basket. The kitchen used 54 apples for a crumble that afternoon. The rest were shared equally between 3 market boxes, and Nadia took the first box to the stall. She sold 17 apples from that box before the rain started. The orchard has 64 trees. How many apples are left in Nadia's box?
A business had 27 items. They added 50. They multiplied by 5. They added 45. They removed 334. They added 16. They worked 60 minutes, or 1 hour. They removed 73. How many items?

Grandpa Sal has 55 dollars in his coin jar, worth exactly 5,500 cents when he counts it out loud with his grandkids. He adds 69 more dollars from a garage sale over the weekend. A birthday check from his brother adds 70 more dollars. He adds 12 more dollars from returning some soda cans. His son, Tony, mentions his own savings account has 900 dollars, way more than what's in Grandpa Sal's jar. A matching contribution from his wife brings the jar to 2 times what it was. The corner store, separately, restocked 200 candy bars that same week. He then spends 31 dollars on a new fishing rod. A pension bonus brings the jar to 3 times what it had left. How much money is in Grandpa Sal's coin jar now?

A collector had 148 cards. They multiplied by 6 through purchasing (morning). They multiplied by 2 through trading (afternoon). They multiplied by 2 through another round. They multiplied by 9 for bulk inventory. Alex had 1000 cards but wasn't counted. Sarah had 500 cards also separate. After morning and afternoon activities but before the second afternoon round, how many cards after each of the first two multiplications?

In the morning 4 lorries arrived at the building site, each carrying 8 pallets with 196 bricks on every pallet, and the bricklayers used 4896 bricks before lunch. The site is 15 kilometres from the brickworks. In the afternoon a labourer found 37 bricks in an old skip and added them to the stock, and 21 bricks were broken by a forklift. In the evening the foreman sold every brick left in the stock to a neighbouring site at 6 cents a brick. How many cents did the foreman receive?

A museum operates through the day. They start with 77 artifacts in the morning. They multiply by 9 to forecast nine galleries. They multiply by 8 for an eight-month exhibition. They lose 5450 artifacts to scheduled deaccessioning. They add 17 artifacts from new acquisitions. They add 39 more artifacts from donations. Converting to dozens, what is their exhibition count?

The regional seed bank started the spring with 180 paper packets of sunflower seed, and 41 further packets arrived from a partner bank. Each packet held 9 seeds, and the staff then found 74 loose seeds at the bottom of the storage bin and added them to the count. The garden log records growth in millimetres rather than in centimetres. Every seed that was sown came up as a plant bearing 3 flower heads, and each flower head opened with 7 outer petals. How many outer petals were there in the whole trial plot?

A group had 161 members. In the morning, 123 left. By midday, 36 more departed. The remaining quadrupled by afternoon. By evening, it tripled. His associate managed 85 people. When converted to 3-person units (unit conversion), how many final units?

A grocery store had 215 cans. They added 60 cans to inventory. They arranged displays with 7 times as many cans. They removed 1734 cans for sale. They restocked 122 more cans later. They donated 68 cans to a food bank. Each can was marked at cents per unit (prices separate from count). How many cans remain?

In the morning, a lemonade stand had 36 dollars in its cash box, or 3,600 cents as the kids liked to count it out. By midday, a busy morning added 56 more dollars. In the afternoon, a matching donation from a parent tripled the cash box. By evening, a tip jar added 11 more dollars. That night, the family paid 206 dollars for new supplies. The next morning, a franchise deal multiplied the remaining cash ninefold. Later that day, a 25-dollar fee was paid to a permit office. How much money was in the cash box?
Two colleagues tracked time in the morning. One had 186 hours. They removed 57, then 42, multiplied by 6, added 69, added 68, and added 78 more. Converting to days, how many?

A team started with 113 points. They gained 71 points in the first match. They multiplied their score 5 times for a tournament multiplier. They scored 375 more points. Finally, they earned 39 bonus points. What is the team's final score?

A business started with 235 dollars. They multiplied by 5 for growth projection. They divided by 5 (returning to original). They subtracted 138 for overhead. They subtracted 90 more for supplies. They multiplied by 2 for future value. A competitor's budget was 1000 dollars separately. After multiplication/division and first subtraction but before the second subtraction, using a unit change (dollars to cents), how much?
A warehouse had 108 items. They removed 6. They divided by 3. They removed 20. How many items?

A tile-maker loaded 98 racks into the kiln, and each rack held 5 tiles. A neighbouring workshop sent 77 finished tiles to join the batch, and 26 more were salvaged from an old order. A big hotel contract then tripled the number of tiles in the store. During transport 233 tiles were cracked and thrown away. The workshop's delivery van has done 64000 miles. How many tiles does the tile-maker have now?

In the morning, a food pantry had 101 boxes of pasta on the shelf. By midday, a grocery donation added 78 more boxes. In the afternoon, a school food drive added 32 more boxes. The pantry director mentioned that 20 extra grocery bags were also donated, though that had nothing to do with the pasta box count. That evening, 106 boxes were distributed to families in need. Right before closing, a late donation added 12 more boxes. How many boxes of pasta were on the shelf after the late donation?

A student had 194 pages (morning reading goal). They added 27 (morning assignment). They subtracted 197 for incomplete sections (mid-morning). They added 21 more (afternoon). They added 7 bonus pages (evening). Time: morning/afternoon/evening. Using 'one distractor' (textbook has 500 pages). Tom and Lisa studied together (named). After addition and subtraction but before afternoon reading, how many pages in the mid-morning?

On Sunday morning a hostel had 62 clean sheets and sent 14 of them away to be mended. The rest were divided equally between 2 floors. During the afternoon the laundry delivered 40 sheets to the ground floor. In the early evening a hotel lent that floor 17 more. Later that night 4 of the ground floor's sheets were ruined by a leaking radiator. How many sheets does the ground floor have?

A charity had 211 dollars, or 21,100 cents as the treasurer liked to note, in its account at the start of the drive. A local business donated 34 more dollars. A matching-donor event then multiplied the account sevenfold. A second matching event multiplied it fourfold again. Finally, the charity spent 3,655 dollars on a community center renovation. How much money was left in the account?

A food bank started the morning with 145 pounds of rice in storage. By midmorning, 120 pounds were distributed to local families. The remaining rice was then repackaged into 8 equally sized batches for a partner shelter, and the total delivered equaled all 8 batches combined. In the afternoon, a grocery store donated 8 more pounds, and later that day a farm delivered 27 more pounds. Since the food bank logs weight in pounds but its national report converts everything to kilograms, staff always double-checked the numbers before submitting it. By evening, a final donation added 74 more pounds. How many pounds of rice did the food bank have by evening?
Two friends compared. One had 55 dollars. Removed 28. Multiplied by 5. By 9. Lost 167 expense. How much remains?

A factory had 196 items. They tripled (multiplied by 3). They divided by 6 for packaging. They multiplied by 3 more for batch scaling. They multiplied by 7 for production runs. They multiplied by 9 for annual projection. A competitor produced 5000 items, using 'double' as a word quantity. After tripling but before the division, how many items?
